clue.text: Wrecker cast boat user adrift

indicators.note: cast can mean thrown about or moulded afresh, so the letters take a new shape
something adrift has come loose and wanders, so these letters float out of their order

explanation.surface: A wrecker sets a boat-user loose to drift at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A saboteur deliberately damages or destroys things, so he is a wrecker in the destructive sense.

clue.text: Part of vehicle to wear out, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is a word spoken, so the spelling of the answer may differ from the word meant

parts.note: to tire is to wear out

explanation.surface: A vehicle part that wears out, so people say.
explanation.walkthrough: TYRE is the British spelling of the American 'tire'; the two sound identical.
explanation.definitionFit: A tyre is the rubber covering on a wheel, one component of a car or bike.

clue.text: Comic almost dead in cart

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter of the word is dropped

explanation.surface: A comedian nearly expires while riding in a cart.
explanation.walkthrough: WAGGON is an older British spelling of wagon.
explanation.definitionFit: A waggon is a four-wheeled vehicle for carrying goods, a kind of cart.

clue.text: Great queen, say, backing Russian goldsmith

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the abbreviation for 'say' is read in reverse

explanation.surface: A grand queen is supporting a Russian jeweller.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Carl Fabergé was the Russian goldsmith famous for jewelled eggs made for the tsars.

clue.text: European bridge raid organised

indicators.note: something organised has been arranged afresh, so these letters are put in a new order

parts.note: a span is a bridge, or the stretch it crosses

explanation.surface: A European plans an organised attack on a bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: A Spaniard is a native of Spain, a European country.

clue.text: Special performance of group work

parts.note: a party is a group of people
a piece is a work of art or music

explanation.surface: A band gives a special performance of one of its compositions.
explanation.definitionFit: A party piece is the turn someone habitually performs to entertain others at gatherings.

clue.text: Endless fast before he finds something to eat

indicators.note: endless means without its end, so the last letter is cut off

explanation.surface: After a long fast, a man finally finds food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast' looks like going without food, which suits the surface, but it means quick.
explanation.definitionFit: A quiche is a savoury egg tart, so it is food in a deliberately vague description.

clue.text: Paul finally given day off to silence a pop star

indicators.note: off suggests gone wrong or out of order, so the letters are scrambled
finally points to the very end of the name, so only its closing letter is used

explanation.surface: Paul is given a day off work to keep a pop singer quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: Lady Gaga is an American singer famous for chart pop hits such as Poker Face.

clue.text: Pestilence in city that's changed hands

indicators.note: hands are right and left, so the letter for one hand is swapped for the letter for the other

explanation.surface: Disease breaks out in a city whose ownership has passed to someone else.
explanation.walkthrough: R for right becomes L for left, turning PRAGUE into PLAGUE.
explanation.definitionFit: A plague is an epidemic of deadly disease, which is what pestilence means.

clue.text: Polish sweetheart who's not all there!

indicators.note: not all there means incomplete, so the word is missing its final letter

parts.note: honey is a term of endearment

explanation.surface: A Polish girlfriend who is a bit dim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' looks like a nationality thanks to the capital letter; it is the verb to polish.
explanation.definitionFit: To hone is to sharpen or refine, as you polish a skill or blade.

clue.text: Type of fracture in broken tiger's neck

indicators.note: broken things lie in pieces, so these letters are reassembled in another order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged, the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A vet diagnoses a fracture in a tiger's broken neck.
explanation.definitionFit: A greenstick fracture is a partial break where the bone bends and cracks on one side, common in children.

clue.text: The broadcast featured Iranian city

indicators.note: broadcast also means scattered, as seed is sown, so the letters are spread into a new order

parts.note: a paper that ran a story featured it

explanation.surface: A television broadcast showed an Iranian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast featured' reads as one phrase about television, but broadcast scatters the word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Tehran is the capital and largest city of Iran.

clue.text: Animal overcoming restraining device that's badly constructed

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: A beast breaks free of a poorly made restraint.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, one piece 'overcoming' another sits above it, so the animal comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Ramshackle describes a building or structure so poorly made it looks ready to collapse.

clue.text: Struggles with gross fruit

explanation.surface: Someone battles with disgusting fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gross' looks like disgusting, but it is the trade measure of twelve dozen, abbreviated GR.
explanation.definitionFit: To grapple is to wrestle or fight at close quarters, so it means struggle.

clue.text: Formidable expert exhibits look of disgust

parts.note: an ace is a highly skilled person

explanation.surface: A daunting specialist pulls a face of distaste.
explanation.definitionFit: A grimace is a twisted facial expression showing pain, disgust or disapproval.

clue.text: Soldier in company with married man at party

explanation.surface: A soldier and a married man keep company at a party.
explanation.definitionFit: A commando is a member of an elite military unit trained for raids.

clue.text: Hostile commercial against Gaelic

parts.note: Erse is an old name for Scottish or Irish Gaelic

explanation.surface: An advert attacking the Gaelic language provokes hostility.
explanation.definitionFit: Adverse conditions or reactions work against you, so they are unfavourable or hostile.

clue.text: South Australia and New Guinea endlessly optimistic

indicators.note: endlessly means without an end, so the place name loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Two southern-hemisphere places are forever hopeful.
explanation.definitionFit: Sanguine means cheerfully confident about the future, i.e. hopeful.

clue.text: Maria, heartless damsel, mistreated sailor

indicators.note: mistreated means handled badly, so the letters are knocked out of order
heartless means its inside is removed, so only the outermost letters of the word stay

parts.note: first and last letters of damsel

explanation.surface: Maria, a cold-hearted young woman, treated a sailor badly.
explanation.definitionFit: An admiral is a naval officer of the highest rank, so a sailor in the broad sense.

clue.text: Measured ham fed to cuckoo

indicators.note: cuckoo means crazy, so the letters go wild and rearrange

explanation.surface: A measured portion of ham is fed to a cuckoo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cuckoo' reads as a bird being fed, but it means crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: To fathom water is to measure its depth in fathoms, so fathomed means measured.

clue.text: A rector's article on rodent found on Turkish mountain

explanation.surface: A vicar writes about a rat discovered on a mountain in Turkey.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'on' puts the article above the rodent.
explanation.definitionFit: Mount Ararat in eastern Turkey is where Noah's Ark is said to have come to rest.

clue.text: Gathers second part of harvest in valleys

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: glens are narrow valleys, especially in Scotland

indicators.note: second part picks out the letter in position two of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Collects the rest of the harvest in the valleys.
explanation.definitionFit: To glean is to gather leftover grain after reaping, or gather information bit by bit.

clue.text: Oily Greek's sexually available

explanation.surface: A slippery Greek is said to be easy.
explanation.definitionFit: Greasy means covered in or like grease, hence oily.

clue.text: China cares about sweet stuff

indicators.note: about means turned around or here and there, so the letters move into a new order

explanation.surface: China is concerned about sugary things.
explanation.definitionFit: Saccharine is an artificial sweetener, or anything sugary-sweet.

clue.text: Go out without heart condition

indicators.note: without heart means the middle is taken away, so the central letter goes

explanation.surface: Leave without courage.
explanation.definitionFit: Gout is a painful medical condition caused by uric acid crystals in the joints.

clue.text: Aim of lass to capture boy's heart

indicators.note: capturing means holding something inside, so one piece goes within the other
the heart of a word is its middle, so only the central letter is kept

explanation.surface: A girl's ambition is to win a boy's love.
explanation.definitionFit: A goal is an objective you are aiming for.

clue.text: Judge became unwell, locked up

explanation.surface: A judge fell ill and was imprisoned.
explanation.definitionFit: Jailed means put in prison, i.e. locked up.

clue.text: Sailor with spots chooses not to vote

explanation.surface: A sailor with a rash decides to sit out the election.
explanation.definitionFit: To abstain is to deliberately refrain from casting a ballot in an election.
